study.title: Acupuncture decreases amygdala functional connectivity in subjective tinnitus
study.population: Twenty-six patients with subjective tinnitus and twenty-six age- and gender-matched healthy controls (HC)
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) history of craniocerebral trauma; (2) those unsuitable for MRI (such as internal metal implants); (3) intracranial lesions such as tumors, hemorrhage and infarction detected after MRI

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: acupoints on the affected side of tinnitus (SI19, TE17, GB12, GB8), distal bilateral acupoints (TE3, TE5) and the Governor Vessel acupoints (GV20, GV26, GV15)
interventions.laterality_exact: affected side for SI19, TE17, GB12, GB8; bilateral for TE3, TE5; midline for GV20, GV26, GV15
interventions.manipulation_exact: the acupuncturist manipulated the needle for obtaining the deqi sensation (acid, numbness, swelling and pain); SI19 was needle-inserted into with the mouth open
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; deqi sensation (acid, numbness, swelling and pain)

extraction_notes.note: No quantitative deqi measurement was reported. Deqi is mentioned only qualitatively as a desired endpoint ('acid, numbness, swelling and pain') in the intervention description. No deqi scale (e.g., MASS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire) was used or reported.

No expectancy, credibility, or blinding assessment was reported. The study has no sham control arm, so blinding success is not applicable for patient-sham comparisons, but no expectancy measure was reported for the acupuncture group either.
Adverse events were not reported anywhere in the manuscript.

Clinical outcome data (THI, TEQ, VAS) are presented only as violin plots in Figure 2. No means, standard deviations, medians, or exact p-values per scale are reported in text or tables. The statistical test used for pre-post comparison is not stated.
extraction_notes.source_location: Page 5, Figure 2 and Clinical symptoms section

extraction_notes.note: Inclusion criteria for tinnitus patients are not explicitly listed. Exclusion criteria are listed but apply to all participants. No formal inclusion criteria (e.g., minimum tinnitus duration, audiological criteria) are reported.
The abstract mentions 'VSA score' but all other parts of the paper refer to 'VAS score'. This appears to be a typographical error in the abstract. Extracted as VAS throughout.

It is not completely clear whether HC underwent any sham or parallel procedure, or were simply scanned twice without any treatment. The paper states 'Data of rs-fMRI for all subjective tinnitus patients as well as HC were collected before and after acupuncture' but does not describe what HC did between scans.

The linear regression models use FC extracted from regions with significant group differences. It is not entirely clear which specific FC value(s) was extracted for the regression (e.g., from which cluster, which contrast, which brain region). The paper states 'The FC of brain regions with significant differences in subjective tinnitus patients was extracted' without specifying which contrast or cluster.

The linear regression scatter plots in Figures 6 and 7 show equation and R2 values within the figure. These were transcribed as reported in the figure captions and visible equations. Numeric values from scatter plots may have limited precision.
No trial registration number is provided. The study is described as a case-control study with pre-post assessments but was not registered as a clinical trial per available information.

The THI regression is described as non-significant (p > 0.05) in the results text but Table 4 in the paper does not include a row for THI, only TEQ and VAS rows. The non-significant THI result is mentioned only in narrative.
extraction_notes.source_location: Page 6, Linear regression between clinical symptoms of tinnitus and FC section; Table 4

extraction_notes.note: The flip angle for rs-fMRI is listed as 90° and field of view as 256 × 256 mm2 with matrix size 64 × 64 in the acquisition parameters. The structural scan has different parameters. These have been transcribed separately but the paper lists them in a single paragraph.

Participant demographic data (exact ages, sex distribution per arm) are stated as: tinnitus group 14 females, mean age 45.2 ± 11.45; HC 14 females, age 46.3 ± 12.82. It is not clear if the age is mean ± SD or mean ± SE; assumed SD based on convention.

The n_analyzed for contrasts 1 and 2 (two-sample t-tests between tinnitus and HC) is inferred as 52 (26 tinnitus + 26 HC). The paper does not state this explicitly in the results, only in the Participants section.
extraction_notes.source_location: Page 2, Participants section; Pages 4-6, Statistical analysis and Results sections
